name: Question 14
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$  select the correct options in the computations of the matrix $U$ below.From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce the singular values ${\sigma }_{1}=\sqrt{6}$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=0.$

Now, we compute the $1$st column of $U.$ It is given by:

|  |  | {{field-1}} |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${u}_{1}=\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
|  |  | $-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ |  |  |

Since the second singular value is ${\sigma }_{2}=0$, and we do not have the third singular value, we can't use the same formula to find the second and third columns of $U.$ But we know that $U$ must be orthogonal.

Hence, we must find vectors $u=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}]^{T}$ such that ${u}_{1}\cdot u=0,$ which is equivalent to

$$
{{field-3}}.
$$
